samples.summary: Whitespace-only `src` passes the emptiness guard and renders a broken image
samples.evidence: `if (src === undefined || src === '') return false;` only rejects the exactly-empty string. `` yields src=` ` after `unescapeAll`, which `normalizeLink` percent-encodes to `%20%20%20` and `validateLink` accepts (no bad proto), so the rule succeeds and emits ``. The browser then issues a request for a relative URL and shows a broken-image icon, where the previous behaviour (and the plugin's stated 'decline and show the source as text' contract) would have left the tag visible as text. A `src.trim() === ''` check would close it.

samples.summary: `height` is accepted and emitted but is a silent no-op under the app's CSS, the exact failure mode the design says it refuses to create
samples.evidence: `if (height !== undefined && !DIMENSION_RE.test(height)) return false;` / line 156 pushes `['height', height]`. Tailwind preflight (packages/frontend/src/index.css:1 `@import "tailwindcss"`) ships `img { max-width: 100%; height: auto }`, and an author CSS declaration outranks the presentational hint from an HTML dimension attribute. So `` renders at intrinsic size with no hint why — precisely the outcome the plugin's own rationale ("Declining rather than dropping the offending attribute is deliberate: silently ignoring `style="width:200px"` would render at intrinsic size with no hint why") cites as unacceptable. It is acknowledged as a caveat in docs/design/notes/notes.md:460, so this is a known-but-shipped behavioural gap rather than an oversight.

samples.summary: The rule still slices the remaining inline chunk per `<img` occurrence, so the quadratic behaviour the comment claims to avoid is only narrowed, not removed
samples.evidence: `startsImgTag`'s doc comment (lines 114-118) says slicing "the rest of the chunk each time would be quadratic in a long note", but line 132 does exactly that — `state.src.slice(state.pos, state.posMax)` — for every position that begins with `<img`. A note consisting of many repeated `<img` fragments (each refused, so parsing continues) performs O(n) slices of O(n) each, i.e. O(n²) work on a keystroke-driven re-render (preview.render runs per keystroke). Impact is limited to pathological/adversarial content; the fix is to bound the slice (e.g. to the next `>` or a fixed max tag length).

samples.summary: Two real-world tag shapes are refused by the attribute scanner: an unquoted URL containing `=`, and a space between `/` and `>`
samples.evidence: `ATTR_RE`'s unquoted-value class `[^\s"'`=<>]+` excludes `=`, so `` parses as value `a.png?w` with a trailing `=1` that fails the `region.slice(cursor).trim() !== ''` check at line 108 and is refused. Likewise ``: IMG_TAG_RE's `\s*\/?>` cannot match `/ >`, so the group swallows the `/` into the attribute region and line 108 rejects it. Both fall through to escaped text — safe and consistent with the 'decline' policy, but they are valid HTML the doc's "unquoted values … all parse" claim implies will work.
